detailed_findings.finding: Existence is complete: Bézout yields x with kx + py = 1, reduction mod p gives an inverse, and taking the remainder mod p places the witness in {1,...,p-1} after excluding 0.
Uniqueness is complete: from ka ≡ kb ≡ 1 (mod p), the proof derives p | k(a-b), uses gcd(k,p)=1 via Bézout to conclude p | (a-b), and then uses the range of a-b to force a=b.

reason: The proof correctly establishes gcd(k,p)=1 from primality and 1 ≤ k ≤ p-1, uses Bézout to obtain an inverse modulo p, normalizes that inverse to the representative set {1,...,p-1}, and proves uniqueness by showing any two such representatives differ by a multiple of p and hence must be equal. It matches the lemma and supports the root theorem’s definition of the inverse map I.
